question.worked_solution:
First, note that the index $n$ starts from $3,$ and so the sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of this geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

Computing the first few terms, we get:

$$
{a}_{3}=6{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{3-2}=6(-\frac{1}{5})=-\frac{6}{5}
$$

$$
{a}_{4}=6{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{4-2}=6(\frac{1}{25})=\frac{6}{25}.
$$

Therefore, the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{4}}{{a}_{3}}=\frac{(\frac{6}{25})}{(-\frac{6}{5})}=-\frac{1}{5}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }6{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{\,n-2} & =\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{6}{5})}{1-(-\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =-\frac{(\frac{6}{5})}{(\frac{6}{5})} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
